questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

text:
Hello,

I'll be honest from the start: I never filed any claim for compensation against Hagenbuch Management Ltd, not with a court and not with the conciliation office. At the time I just wanted to move on, and nobody told me there might be a deadline.

My notice period with them ended at the end of July 2025 and I left on 31 July.

I don't think the notice had anything to do with me asking for something. I had never made any demands on them, not for overtime, not for a raise, nothing. That's not why they let me go.

In June 2025 I wrote to Noah Tanner, the director, and asked him to give me the reasons for the notice in writing. I sent it as a registered letter from the post office in Altdorf.

The notice itself he gave me at the end of May 2025, in a short meeting in his office, with a one-page letter.

So my job ended more than nine months ago. The reason I'm writing now is that on 2 April 2026 I ran into my old colleague Mark Keller, who told me the company has since hired two new people for exactly my job. That made me angry all over again, and I wonder whether there is still anything I can do after all this time.

I earned CHF 1,330 a month, part-time. I'd be grateful for an honest answer, even if it's that it's too late.

Best regards,
Leo Gisler
Bahnhofstrasse 108, Altdorf
